text: To understand how PPS spends [music]
money, it helps to picture three
buckets. The first and most important
bucket is the [music] general fund. This
pays for day-to-day operations like
teacher salaries, school staff,
classroom [music] supplies,
transportation, and utilities. For 2526
school year, that bucket is about $868
million. The second bucket is [music]
the special revenue fund. This bucket is
restricted, meaning that those dollars
can only be used [music] for specific
activities or groups of students. It
includes things like state and federal
grants, local donations, [music] and the
student nutrition program. This year,
PPS is planning for about $225 million
in special revenue. The third bucket is
bond [music] funds. These funds can only
be used for major construction and
capital projects, [music] renovating
schools, updating technology, or making
seismic upgrades. Bond dollars are voter
approved and legally [music] cannot be
used to pay teacher salaries or school
operations. Knowing which funds [music]
can be used for what is key to
understanding school finance.
